Draw the panels sharing one colour scale as a single ggplot

Source: R/feature_plots.R
feature_ggplot.Rd

Draw the panels sharing one colour scale as a single ggplot

Usage

feature_ggplot(
  members,
  colour_scale,
  strip,
  strip.face,
  facet_ncol,
  facet_nrow,
  facet_dir,
  geom,
  order,
  center,
  pt.size,
  alpha,
  outline,
  outline.color,
  outline.size,
  label,
  label.size,
  label.color,
  legend.position,
  legend.direction,
  legend.length,
  legend.width,
  legend.text.size,
  legend.title.face,
  panel.width,
  panel.height,
  panel.spacing,
  strip.text.size,
  rd,
  raster,
  raster.threshold,
  raster.dpi,
  bg,
  halo.color,
  seed,
  arrow.scale = 1
)

Arguments

members

Panels to draw, each with its `cells`, `marks` and `label`

colour_scale

Resolved colour scale, from resolve_colour_scale

strip

Whether to label the panels with a strip

strip.face

Font face of the strip text

facet_ncol, facet_nrow, facet_dir

Facet layout

geom

How values are drawn: "point" (default) colours each cell; "hex" colours hexagonal tiles by a summary of the cells in them (see `hex.fun`); "density" colours each cell by values smoothed over neighbouring cells (see `density.method`)

order

Whether to draw cells with higher values on top, default is TRUE; on a diverging scale, cells further from the centre are drawn on top. If FALSE, cells are drawn in random order

center

Centre of a diverging scale, default is 0. The two sides of the scale extend equally far in colour from the centre, so that a side with a smaller range does not reach its darkest colour

pt.size

Point size, default is 0.3

alpha

Point (or tile) transparency, default is 1

outline

Whether to draw an outline around the cell clouds, default is FALSE. Not used for `geom = "hex"`

outline.color

Colour of the outline, default is "black"

outline.size

Thickness of the outline (in point size units), default is 0.6

label

Whether to label groups at their median position, default is FALSE. Groups are the active identities unless `label.by` is given

label.size

Size of the group labels in mm, default is 3.5

label.color

Colour of the group labels, default is "black"

legend.position

Position of the legend, one of "right" (default), "left", "top", "bottom", "inside" or "none"

legend.direction

Direction of the colour bar, "vertical" or "horizontal". If NULL (default), horizontal for top and bottom legends and vertical otherwise

legend.length

Length of the colour bar in inches, default is 1.5

legend.width

Thickness of the colour bar in inches, default is 0.15

legend.text.size

Font size of the legend text and title in points. If NULL (default), the theme's base size (11)

legend.title.face

Font face of the legend title. "auto" (default) sets it in bold, gene names in bold italics

panel.width

Width of a single panel in inches, default is 4

panel.height

Height of a single panel in inches, default is `panel.width`

panel.spacing

Gap between panels in inches, default is 0.1

strip.text.size

Font size of the panel labels in points. If NULL (default), the theme's large size (12)

rd

Output of reduction_data

raster

Whether to rasterize the points while keeping text, legend and arrows as vectors: NULL (default) rasterizes when there are more than `raster.threshold` cells, or TRUE / FALSE. Hex tiles are always drawn as vectors

raster.threshold

Number of cells above which `raster = NULL` rasterizes, default is 10000

raster.dpi

Resolution of the rasterized points, default is 1000. Match the `dpi` used when saving raster (e.g. png) output

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent", so that the figure can be placed on any background (gaps inside outlines and label halos are then white). Use e.g. "white" for an opaque background

halo.color

Colour of the gap inside outlines and of label halos

seed

Random seed used for drawing order and label placement, default is 42. The global random number generator state is not changed

arrow.scale

The `arrow.scale` of the dimension arrows, which sets the room left for their labels

Value

a ggplot object
